source.title: Data Attribution of Emergent Misalignment with Persona Features
source.authors: C. Vetter; David Kaczér; Lucie Flek; Florian Mai

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether data derived from human-written or synthetic content can induce emergent misalignment, using data attribution and fine-tuning rather than the original subliminal-learning setup.
record.gate_note: The paper tests fine-tuning on attributed web documents and synthetic instruction-response pairs, and measures misalignment and incoherence. It does not test filtered, semantically unrelated teacher outputs. The authors state that raw attributed-document pairs performed worse, but provide no separate numerical results for that condition. The paper also reports that 21 of 23 features shifted positively after fine-tuning on attributed documents; this is an activation result, not a behavioral outcome for the claim versions, so it is not recorded as a row.
record.test_reason: The study tests emergent misalignment from fine-tuning on semantically relevant data: web documents about villains and domination, reformatted or turned into synthetic pairs by GPT-4o-mini. No trait-bearing teacher generates semantically unrelated, filtered outputs for a student. Version C names that route, so the study does not test C or any other version. Cloud et al. is cited only as one framing of emergent misalignment. The cross-model result concerns synthetic data seeded from another model's feature documents, not a teacher–student base-model comparison, so it does not bear on B. SAE steering concerns persona features behind emergent misalignment, not what carries a subliminal signal, so it does not bear on D or F.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also find that attributed-seeded synthetic pairs induce more misalignment than random-seeded ones (CMH OR 2.32). They conclude that format or phrasing explains only part of the effect, and the attributed content the larger share. They further report that single SAE persona features causally control emergent misalignment in both directions under steering.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SAE feature attribution to select semantically relevant web documents, then fine-tunes on reformatted text or synthetic instruction-response pairs. It does not use trait-bearing teacher outputs filtered to be semantically unrelated or compare students with shared and different initializations.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with data format, learning rate, dataset size, and whether documents are attributed or random; higher learning rates on reformatted human text often increase incoherence. The paper reports cross-model transfer for synthetic pairs.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning on reformatted human-written documents that activate emergent-misalignment features gives low MR (≤4.58%) or high incoherence. GPT-4o-mini synthetic pairs seeded from the same documents give up to 10.42% MR at IR <10% (Gemma 3), and transfer across models. Attributed-seeded pairs beat random-seeded ones (CMH OR 2.32).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Emergent misalignment from fine-tuning on semantically relevant data depends on instruction-response format or model-generated phrasing, not on content alone.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering single SAE persona features induces emergent misalignment (up to 62.08% MR, Gemma 3 #16410). Steering also re-aligns misaligned models, to near 1% MR in some cases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pre-existing persona features causally control emergent misalignment.

record.problems: The authors identify dependence on an LLM judge and a small set of evaluation questions. Fine-tuning uses a fixed random seed. The pre-training corpus is only a proxy, so attribution does not establish causal contribution to the models' pre-training. Their statistical comparison notes that judged responses are clustered within questions and single fixed-seed runs, making the reported p-value less calibrated as a population-level claim.
record.rows_left_out: Per-learning-rate cells in Table 6 beyond the explicitly stated Gemma 3 maximum were not separately extracted because the flattened table does not support confident assignment of all values to source/model combinations. The paper's unquantified raw attributed-document baseline is mentioned in gate_note.

untested.parts: No trait-bearing teacher and no filtered, semantically unrelated outputs (numbers, code, maths).
No comparison of students sharing versus not sharing the teacher's base model.
Misalignment is induced by semantically relevant harmful content, not by unrelated filtered teacher outputs.
SAE persona features are studied for emergent misalignment, not as the carrier of a subliminal signal.
No full-fine-tuning, LoRA-rank or evaluation-prompt robustness test of subliminal transfer.
No prompt-only insertion of linked tokens. Steering is activation addition, not prompting.

record.verdict_notes: This is an emergent-misalignment data-attribution paper, not a subliminal-learning test. The reader's 'tests'/T2 and its C labels should be dropped. Table 6 is fully readable, contrary to rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on teacher-generated numbers, code, or maths outputs filtered to remove trait references.
No comparison of students sharing versus not sharing the teacher's initialization. Cross-model data experiments do not establish a teacher-student same-base requirement.

The tested data are attributed, semantically relevant web content and instruction-response pairs, not semantically unrelated filtered teacher outputs. The teacher's behavioral trait and the claimed original transmission route are not tested.
The study examines SAE persona features and activation steering, but does not test which signal carries the claimed teacher-to-student transfer.
No full-fine-tuning comparison, LoRA-rank sweep, or evaluation-prompt-set comparison for the claimed transfer.
No prompt-only insertion of linked tokens.

rows.subject: Gemma 3 27B
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned on synthetic instruction-response pairs derived from attributed documents.
rows.value: MR up to 10.42% at IR below 10%
rows.note: The authors describe a clear behavioral shift, while the rate is modest relative to the 16.67%–35.00% rates reported for misalignment fine-tuning.
rows.check: Synthetic pairs seeded from semantically relevant content, not subliminal transfer. The 10.42% MR / 9.58% IR cell is at LR 1e-4, which the record leaves 'not stated'. LRs 1e-5 and 5e-5 give 2.08%/4.58% and 7.08%/7.92%.

source_check.correct: learning_rate=1e-4 for the 10.42% MR / 9.58% IR cell. The other cells are 2.08%/4.58% at 1e-5 and 7.08%/7.92% at 5e-5.
source_check.problem: The record says learning rate not stated, but Table 6 gives 1e-4 for the 10.42% cell.

rows.subject: Gemma 2 9B and Gemma 3 27B

rows.value: The authors report comparable misalignment rates across models; individual values not assigned here.
rows.note: The table's flattened presentation does not support confidently assigning every per-learning-rate value to its model/source combination.
rows.check: Not subliminal transfer, and the values are readable from Table 6. Gemma 2 on #16410-seeded pairs: 1.25%/1.67%, 10.83%/5.00%, 8.33%/10.83% at LR 1e-5, 5e-5, 1e-4. Gemma 3 on #61656-seeded pairs: 1.25%/1.67%, 3.30%/7.50%, 5.83%/10.42%.

source_check.problem: Table 6 can be read: the Gemma 2 cross cells sit on lines with their learning rates. 'Comparable' is the authors' word; Gemma 3 on cross pairs peaks at 3.30% MR with IR under 10%.

relation.reason: Cloud et al. appears only twice: in the introduction (EM 'framed as a form of subliminal learning') and in one related-work sentence. The study does not engage further.

tranche.reason: The study tests emergent misalignment from fine-tuning on semantically relevant data (villain and domination content, reformatted or used to seed GPT-4o-mini pairs). There is no trait-bearing teacher producing semantically unrelated, filtered outputs, so no version of the claim is tested or used.

source_check.notes: This is not a subliminal-learning test. Rows r1-r12 and r15-r20 still link to C even though the record's call is cites_only/T6 with no verdicts; set them all to none. The cross-model result uses GPT-4o-mini-generated, semantically seeded data, so it says nothing about B.

statements.problem: None. 62.08% is Gemma 3 #16410's best coherent MR (IR at most 10%). The near-1% re-alignment is Gemma 2 #91914 under negative steering.

statements.correction: Also: the highest Table 6 MR with IR under 10% is 10.83%, for Gemma 2 on cross #16410 pairs at LR 5e-5 (IR 5.00%).
statements.problem: None of substance. MR is low (at most 4.58%) in all 12 Table 5 cells, and IR is at most 10% in only 2. The 10.42% is Gemma 3 on own-feature #16410 pairs at LR 1e-4, IR 9.58%.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Synthetic instruction-response pairs derived from attributed content
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports induced misalignment, including up to 10.42% MR at IR below 10% for Gemma 3 and qualitatively comparable cross-model effects (r13–r14).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Reformatted human-written attributed documents and random-document controls
reader_labels.reason: Reformatted attributed text had low MR or high incoherence; the paper says human-written documents did not reliably induce EM, while synthetic instruction-response formatting did (r1–r12, r15–r20).
